central_claim.note: Conservative booster half of C1, in the paper's own p.10 wording ('more likely to received booster doses in liberal regions'). Liberals' low hesitancy or high uptake regardless of climate is in the quote but not the claim. 'Moderates' is the paper's framing; not flagged.

evidence.note: Online recruitment of 683 US participants, March 8 to April 19, 2023: E1 without the nonprobability convenience sample or Qualtrics Panels, so partial. Final N without the screening figures (partial E2). Linear and logistic regressions with controls but no interaction term (partial E6). Quote is the abstract.

flags.text: Calls the hesitancy measures 'validated scales'. The paper modified the AAVS items for COVID-19 and took booster items from a 2022 survey; it reports only that the modified items 'demonstrated adequate reliability' after a CFA (p.5), never that the scales are validated.

evidence.note: Hesitancy measures (AAVS, booster items from a 2022 survey); self-reported vaccine and booster status not mentioned. Booster-item source is accurate but not in the gold.

key_findings.note: Liberal half of the hesitancy interaction (low regardless of climate).
Conservative half of the hesitancy interaction; with [0] states F2 in full.

Liberals boosted regardless; conservatives' uptake tied to climate, without the direction. 'Strongly tied' is loose for 'associated with' but the paper calls the booster gap its most striking result (60% vs under 35%); not flagged.

Gives over 65% for the most liberal and under 35% for conservatives in conservative climates, but drops the 60% for conservatives in liberal climates, so the conservative-across-climates contrast that is F3's point is not stated (it is in the quote only). Not joined with [2]: neither entry says conservatives in liberal climates are more likely boosted.
Interaction significant for vaccine hesitancy, booster hesitancy and booster status (p.10), without the shape; credited partial as the earlier judge did for like entries.

scope_and_limits.note: Cross-sectional, so no causal or directional conclusion (L2); self-report open to social desirability and recall bias (L3). The only quote is marked NOT IN PAPER (a splice of p.10 sentences with altered wording), so no credit.
Vote share as a proxy; other regional factors such as population density could drive the associations.

theoretical_positioning.note: Names only the orientation literature (broadened to 'health behavior') and the extension by testing moderation; the quote is the paper's 'first assessment' sentence. Same call as the earlier judge's on the first run.

interlocutor_claim.note: Prior research links conservatism (and conservative climate) to hesitancy and lower vaccination; the paper builds on it (I1, climate part close to I3/I6). The quote is marked NOT IN PAPER ('The present research is consistent' for the paper's 'Our research is consistent'), so no credit. 'Disputes or builds on' hedges the stance; the paper only builds on these findings. Not flagged.
